title: Praying for Your Marriage: Verses for a Hard Season | Prayed
headline: Praying for your marriage, when it is harder than it used to be
dek: Fifteen verses for a marriage in a hard season, arranged around the three prayers that actually help: soften my heart, help us forgive, and hold us together.
desc: Fifteen Bible verses for marriage from the World English Bible, arranged around three prayers for a hard season: soften my own heart, help us forgive each other, and hold us together. With a prayer to write for each.
card: Fifteen verses for a marriage in a hard season: soften my heart, help us forgive, hold us together.
intro: Most prayers for a marriage start out as prayers about the other person. Change him. Make her see. It is natural and it is usually where the praying stalls, because it is a prayer you cannot do anything about. The prayers that change a marriage tend to start closer to home.

The verses below are quoted word for word from the World English Bible and arranged around the three prayers that people in hard seasons say helped: soften my own heart first, help us forgive each other, and hold us together when we cannot hold ourselves. These are not verses about weddings. They are verses for the tenth year, or the twentieth, when the vows are being kept by decision rather than by feeling.
If your marriage is unsafe, none of this is a substitute for getting help. If it is simply hard, read on.

paras: The most useful prayer in a hard marriage is also the least satisfying: that your own heart would be changed. These verses describe love as patient, humble, bearing with. Pray them about yourself before you pray them about your spouse.

verses.note: Put your own name where love is and see which sentence you cannot say. That is the one to pray.
Bearing with one another in love. Not fixing, not winning. Bearing with. Eager to keep the unity, which means the unity is worth effort.
Addressed to husbands, and the last clause is startling: prayers can be hindered by how you treat your wife. Contempt at home reaches further than home.
Above all these things. Walk in love is the instruction that outranks being right.

sections.pray: I have been praying that you would change her. I am going to start with me. Make me patient. Make me kind. Take the contempt out of my voice before it does more damage. Soften my heart toward the person I promised to love.

paras: Every long marriage carries a ledger, and the ledger is the problem. These verses are about forgiveness that is not earned, because the one you are married to will not earn it any more than you will.

verses.note: Even as Christ forgave you. The standard is not what your spouse deserves. It is what you received.
Love covers a multitude of sins. Not one or two. A multitude. It is a verse for the thing you keep bringing up.
What God has joined. The marriage is not only yours to dissolve, which is also why it is not only yours to save.
Many waters cannot quench love. Written about a love that had already been tested. Yours has been too.

sections.pray: We have been keeping score for years. I want to burn the ledger. Help me forgive the thing I have not been able to let go of, the way you forgave me, without waiting for an apology that may not come.

paras: Some seasons are beyond what either of you can fix, and the prayer is simply that the marriage would survive them. These verses describe a bond that is held by something other than the two people in it.

verses.note: A threefold cord. The third strand is the one that does not fray when the other two do.
One flesh. It is a statement of what already is, not a goal to reach. You are already joined. The prayer is to live like it.
Gave himself up for her. The picture of a husband's love is a sacrifice, not a negotiation.
A good thing. Favor of the LORD. On the days it does not feel like either, this verse says what the marriage still is.
Read it again at the end, slowly. Patient. Kind. That is the whole prayer.

sections.pray: We cannot hold this together on our own right now and we both know it. Be the third strand. Hold what we joined when we cannot. Get us through this season to the other side of it, still married, still kind.

closing_h2: Pray for your marriage on a rhythm
closing: A marriage is not an emergency, most of the time. It is a long thing that needs praying for regularly, and the regularity is what most of us fail at. We pray hard in the crisis and not at all in the ordinary months, and then the next crisis arrives with no prayer behind it.

Prayed lets you tag your spouse as a subject and choose a rhythm for them: every day, every week, every month. Every prayer you write for them gathers on one timeline, from the hard season to the better one, and each comes back to you at three days, a week, a month and a year so you can see what changed. Nothing you write leaves your phone, which matters when the prayer is about the person you sleep next to.
Write one prayer for your marriage tonight. Start with your own heart. Set it to come back every week.
